posts.name: DrScott
posts.cooked: This is something of a timing question - Is the taking of damage that would destroy a card a distinct step from actually destroying a card?  I've never really tried to differentiate these two, but I've come across a situation where it matters.  Captain Cosmic's Dynamic Siphon grants use of a power "whenever this card is dealt damage."  It has 2 HP and takes 2 HP of damage, does the use a power ability fire?   Or it is destroyed simultaneously to taking sufficient damage to reduce it's HP to 0 (or below)?
posts.raw: This is something of a timing question - Is the taking of damage that would destroy a card a distinct step from actually destroying a card?  I've never really tried to differentiate these two, but I've come across a situation where it matters.  Captain Cosmic's [i]Dynamic Siphon[/i] grants use of a power "whenever this card is dealt damage."  It has 2 HP and takes 2 HP of damage, does the use a power ability fire?   Or it is destroyed simultaneously to taking sufficient damage to reduce it's HP to 0 (or below)?

posts.name: grysqrl
posts.cooked:
Cards are generally destroyed before their other effects activate, unless those effects specify "when this card is destroyed...". So, constructs that are destroyed by damage will not activate their on-taking-damage effects.

Unless Fixed Point is around, of course.
posts.raw:

That's not how Spiff is playing it.

He's counting the damage as resolving before destruction.  Not saying destruction can't interrupt effects.

Basically destruction can't interrupt the damage that is causing the destuction.

We already know hp goes into negatives, so we know that as hHP is reduced it goes below 0 before triggering destruction.  If the triggering of destruction and the triggering of taking damage reactions are simultaneous, then you could resolve them in either order.

It does lead to interesting post-death combos like the one I had in the app where Unity was incapped by a negative HP Ambuscade, but it would only effect effects that respond to taking damage.

posts.cooked:
I don't know, there is this

https://greaterthangames.com/comment/61044#comment-61044

Quoted also on the document: effects on a destroyed card are in play until the card completes its destruction

In this case it would mean that for example Vitality Conduit would take the last damage necessary to kill it, but before its destruction could be resolved all effects on it would still be in play. Including the effect that triggers because of its taking damage. If merely taking damage enough to trigger destruction was enough to cancel any effect wirtten on a card Akash'Bhuta's Mountainous Carapace would work a little differently than how we know it does, and Infinitor's Ocular Swarm ould make no sense at all.

The Bee Bot / End of Days example is in my opinion a little different because Bee Bot is a second card, interrupting End of Days' resolution with a destruction effect. But with a Construct there's no second card involved in resolution, beyond the one that already damaged it.

Incidentally that could mean that AZ could stay alive after taking that last bit of fire damage with NPCU in play: depends wether bringing his HP up to positives again canceled his damage-triggered destruction or not...

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
The question has an official answer, even if it was from playtesting.

The original donstructs were worded that when they were dealt damage or destroyd their effect happened, and then it was changed to the current wording.

I specifically asked ifthat changed how they worked when damage would destroy them, and Christopher answered that they did change, that when reduced to 0 hp or less they would not trigger because they would leave play first.

 

Playing it differently isn't some horrible crime, it just isn't the official way.  It does create one infinite loop, but it is a rare and difficult one.
